**[named bool] bare true/false as a template argument**

The first template argument of make_llm_executor is the bool parameter Permuted [h/tron/models/common.hpp:80]. A bare false at the use site does not say that the executor is the unpermuted one. The alias tron::host names this exact instantiation [h/tron/models/common.hpp:102], so `model<llm<llm_config, host>>` is the shorter option with no new constant.

Proposed:
```cpp
// file scope (both test cases use it), directly after `namespace {`:
constexpr bool PERMUTED_FALSE = false;  // make_llm_executor<Permuted, ...>

      model<llm<llm_config, make_llm_executor<PERMUTED_FALSE, tensor, tensor, tensor>>>;
```

**[named bool] bare true/false in positional aggregate initialization**

The bare true is the positional initializer of the field writes_kv of attention_operation_descriptor [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:263]. The rule text names constructor calls, not aggregates, so the reviewer decides. The file already builds this struct positionally with bare true/false on about twenty unchanged lines (611, 615, 626, 1240, 1244, ...), so a designated initializer `.writes_kv = true` would be the other way to name it.

```cpp
constexpr bool WRITES_KV_TRUE = true;  // attention_operation_descriptor::writes_kv
```
